number.why: The reported adjusted RR for AAD with S. boulardii versus placebo is 0.29, with 95% CI 0.08–0.98. The ruling correctly identifies adjustment for age and days of cephalosporin use and does not establish the served intention-to-treat label. The stated follow-up supports the study-end window.

quotes.span: Using a multivariate model to adjust for two independent risk factors for AAD (age and days of cephalosporin use), the adjusted relative risk was significantly protective for S. boulardii (RR = 0.29, 95% CI = 0.08, 0.98).
Of the 193 eligible patients, significantly fewer, 7/97 (7.2%), patients receiving S. boulardii developed AAD compared with 14/96 (14.6%) on placebo (p = 0.02).

Lyophilized Saccharomyces boulardii or placebo (1 g/day) was given within 72 h of the start of the antibiotic(s) and continued until 3 days after the antibiotic was discontinued, after which the patients were followed for 7 wk.

entry.why: Hospitalized patients starting beta-lactam antibiotics without acute diarrhea meet the question's entry population of patients receiving antibiotics.

quotes.span: A double-blinded, placebo-controlled, parallel group study was performed in a high-risk group of hospitalized patients receiving a new prescription for a beta-lactam antibiotic and having no acute diarrhea on enrollment.

missed: Nothing additional changes either judgment. Numerical confirmation remains qualified by the ruling's explicit finding that intention-to-treat status is not established.
